items.proofOutline: Choose an intertwiner from the representation to its Frobenius conjugate. It defines the action of a lift of Frobenius and hence of the semidirect Weil group. Schur's lemma makes two such choices scalar; scalar powers are precisely inertial twists. Check continuity on the geometric subgroup.

items.name: Clifford decomposition and the twist stabilizer
items.statement: For irreducible rank-n sigma of W(X1), Fix(sigma) is cyclic of order d|n. Equivalently sigma is induced from a geometrically irreducible rank-n/d representation of W(Xd), whose d geometric Frobenius conjugates are pairwise nonisomorphic. The inducing class is unique up to that orbit. Fix=1 iff geometric restriction is irreducible.

items.name: Correct eigenvalue formula for kappa

items.statement: For a prime p and integer N≥0 define f_p(N)=∏_{1≤i≤N,p∤i}i=N!/[p^floor(N/p) floor(N/p)!]. It is a p-adic unit, including f_p(0)=1. Negative arguments are not admitted.

items.statement: For g≥2,n≥1 there exists a unique P_g,n∈R_g such that #E_n^(F_X^k)=P_g,n(q^k,sigma_1^k,...,sigma_g^k) for every eligible curve and k≥1. items.name: Top weighted term of the counting polynomial
items.statement: Assign degree 2 to t and degree 1 to each z_i. For g≥2, P_g,n has unique top-weight term t^[(g−1)n²+1] with coefficient one; every other monomial has smaller weight. The leading bundle-polynomial term and strict rank-partition weight inequalities must be proved, not inferred from integrality alone.

items.statement: For g≥1,n≥1, A_g,n=I_g,n J_g with J_g=∏(1−z_i)(1−t/z_i), and I_g,n is integral and has the same admissible monomial cone. items.name: Euler specialization of the bundle quotient
items.statement: I_g,n(1,1,...,1)=mu(n)n^(2g−3). The proof imports purity of coprime Higgs moduli, Schiffmann's point-count/Poincare comparison, the nonabelian Hodge comparison with twisted character varieties, and Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas's PGL_n Euler characteristic. items.name: Euler specialization of the local-system quotient
items.statement: For g≥2,n≥1, Q_g,n(1,...,1)=Σ_{d|n}mu(d)mu(n/d)d^(2g−3). The linear part of the trace recurrence is Σ_{d|n}C_d(X1); after division by J and evaluation at one every nonlinear term vanishes. Apply Möbius inversion to item111.

items.name: Low genus and low rank boundary counts
items.statement: For n=1, Q_g,1=1 and P_g,1=J_g. For g=0 or1 and n≥2 there are no irreducible geometric rank-n local systems, so P=Q=0; this uses trivial or abelian geometric fundamental groups. The recurrence dividing by 2g−2 cannot be specialized to g=1.
items.proofOutline: For genus zero the geometric etale fundamental group is trivial; for genus one it is abelian, so characteristic-zero irreducibles have rank one. The rank-one formula is item40. These arguments handle g=1 independently of the singular recurrence denominator.

items.statement: For c=gcd(l_j f_j), c|n and a=Σl_j(l_j−1)f_j/2, delta_e depends only on ord(e mod n). Since 2a=0 mod c, a is zero or the unique element of order two. Thus e+a=0 is detected solely by whether ord(e mod c) is respectively one or two, avoiding the false lcm-of-orders assertion.

items.name: Degree independence of the trace and isocline count
items.statement: For every n≥1 and e,e' with the same order in Z/nZ, J_e=J_e' and P_n^e=P_n^e'. Consequently the geometrically indecomposable bundle count is independent of the degree in the coprime range. Combine cutoff integrals, unitary translation invariance, and item118.

Thus the trace depends only on degree order. Item34 transfers this to isocline bundles and item27 gives the coprime indecomposable consequence.

items.name: Valuation test for distinct exponential sums
items.statement: In a finite extension of Q_p (or a complete algebraically closed extension), take distinct nonzero gamma_i of positive valuation and nonzero integral c_i. Then some k≥1 has Σ c_i gamma_i^−k nonintegral. A Vandermonde system on r successive values bounds the valuations of c_i gamma_i^−k uniformly, contradicting their linear decay.

items.name: Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data
items.statement: For every prime p and genus g≥1 there exists a smooth proper geometrically connected ordinary curve over some F_(p^d) such that p^d,sigma_1,...,sigma_g are multiplicatively independent. For g=1 use Honda–Tate; for g≥2 use the nonempty ordinary locus, full geometric Sp monodromy, a density-one set of mod-l monodromy groups and Chavdarov's sieve with infinitely many auxiliary primes.

items.proofOutline: For g=1 apply item137. For g≥2 restrict the universal family to its nonempty ordinary open, retain full geometric monodromy, use item135 to find a maximal-Weyl fibre, and apply item136. Original sources and the infinitely-many-primes adaptation remain S7.

items.name: Necessity of the admissible Laurent cone
items.statement: Fix a prime p. If P∈Z[t±1,z_i±1] takes integer values on every genus-g smooth proper geometrically connected curve over finite fields of characteristic p, for all choices of paired eigenvalues, every supported monomial t^m z^u satisfies m+Σmin(u_i,0)≥0. Choose the ordinary independent curve, orient the pairs according to negative exponents and apply item120 to its constant extensions.

items.proofOutline: Choose the ordinary independent tuple of item121 and orient each reciprocal pair so its valuation detects the negative exponents in a forbidden monomial. Multiplicative independence separates all evaluated monomials. Across constant extensions, item120 forces a nonintegral value, contradicting the hypothesis.

items.statement: If G is the reductive geometric monodromy group of the semisimple geometric restriction in §2.1, a suitable power of an element normalizing G has its semisimple part inside the group generated by G and scalar/central data as used there. Fix the exact statement of KW01 Theorem3.3(2) before implementing Yu's reduction; the unrestricted assertion for arbitrary algebraic G is not an available theorem.

items.name: Clifford–Mackey induction across constant extensions
items.statement: For the finite-index normal inclusion W(Xd)⊂W(X1), a geometrically irreducible representation with pairwise distinct d conjugates induces irreducibly, and restriction decomposes as their direct sum. Prove continuous finite-dimensional induction, Frobenius reciprocity and the conjugacy criterion on this finite quotient; generic finite-group carrier results alone do not supply the topology.

items.proofOutline: Define induction using finitely many cosets of the normal geometric-constant-extension subgroup, preserving continuity. Compute the restricted representation as the sum of its conjugates. Frobenius reciprocity and pairwise inequivalence show that an endomorphism of the induced representation is scalar and yield the irreducibility criterion in the semisimple setting.

items.name: Harder–Narasimhan existence with shifted slopes
items.statement: For an ordered real T, the T-slope function on saturated subbundles gives a unique Harder–Narasimhan filtration with T-semistable successive quotients and strictly decreasing shifted slopes. Boundedness and the maximal-slope existence proof precede the splitting result.

Its numerator obeys P(z)=q^[(g−1)n²+d]z^[(2g−2)n²+2d]P(1/(qz)), and all roots have absolute value q^−1/2. The disjoint weights in H0,H1,H2 prevent cancellation with the denominator.

The spreading/point-count comparison and cohomological convention must be supplied from Hausel05 and Schiffmann16, not assumed from smoothness.
